If you sell digital products, these are 3 legal documents you need to know about, and most sellers completely overlook number 3 👀 1️⃣ Digital Product Purchase Agreement This can establish the terms of the purchase, including restrictions on sharing or reselling your digital product and other important purchase terms. 2️⃣ Website/Store Terms & Conditions Your Terms & Conditions establish the rules for your online business and can address things like refunds, intellectual property, and limitations of liability. 3️⃣ Content Usage License If a brand or client pays to use your videos, templates, graphics, courses, or other content, a content usage license can clearly define how they can use it, where, for how long, and what happens if they go beyond those rights. Your creativity is an asset. Treat it like one. 💅🏾 And no, you don't necessarily need to spend hundreds on legal fees just to get foundational documents in place. What exactly IS a digital product? Let me break down every type — with examples. If you've been seeing people talk about 'selling digital products' and wondering what they're actually selling — this is for you. A digital product is anything you create once and sell repeatedly — delivered instantly online, no shipping, no inventory, no returns. Here are the main types: 📄 EBOOKS & GUIDES — PDFs that teach something specific. 'Beginner's Guide to Instagram,' '30-Day Content Plan,' 'How to Start Affiliate Marketing.' Sell for $7–$47. Create in Canva for free. 🎨 TEMPLATES — Pre-made designs buyers customize. Instagram templates, planners, resumes, business cards. Sell for $9–$97. Create in Canva. 🎓 COURSES & WORKSHOPS — Video or written lessons teaching a skill. Can sell for $47–$997+. Host on Stan Store or Beacons. 📦 DONE-FOR-YOU PRODUCTS (PLR/MRR) — Products already created that you can resell. Perfect for beginners who aren't ready to create from scratch yet. 📋 PLANNERS, WORKBOOKS & PRINTABLES — Fillable or printable pages. Budget planners, habit trackers, goal workbooks. Sell for $5–$37. These get the most saves and shares on social. The best part? You don't have to create anything to start. You can begin with a done-for-you product while you're still learning — then create your own once you understand what your audience actually wants. Save this. Want to create and sell digital products? Here's what you actually do. 👇  1. Start with a problem. What problem are you solving for someone else? Create the solution. Turn what you know into something useful—a guide, checklist, planner, workbook, template, printable, mini-course, or resource. 3. Choose where to sell it. You can sell digital products through platforms like Etsy, Teachers Pay Teachers, Stan Store, or your own website. Market it. Creating the product is only HALF the job. People have to find it!
